study type: Retrospective cohort study with risk-interval analysis
exposure: Receipt of first dose of measles-containing vaccine
Gestational age at birth (preterm vs full-term)
cohort: The cohort comprised 532,375 children (45,343 preterm and 487,032 full-term) who received their first dose of measles-containing vaccine at 12 to 23 months of age and had no prior history of seizures or seizure-related conditions.
finding: Vaccination with a measles-containing vaccine in the second year of life is associated with a similar relative risk of a first seizure in children born preterm as in those who were born full-term.
followup_time: Up to approximately 25 months after birth (observation period up to 42 days post-vaccination, with vaccinations occurring between 12 and 23 months of age)
